apps.name: Vartagram
apps.subtitle: Telegram-iOS
apps.localizedDescription:
Vartagram Source Code Compilation Guide:

We welcome all developers to use our source code to create applications. There are several things we require from all developers for the moment.

Creating your Telegram Application:

• Please remember to publish your code too in order to comply with the licences.

Adjust Configuration:

• Generate a random identifier:.

• Open Keychain Access and navigate to Certificates. Locate Apple Development: your@email.address (XXXXXXXXXX) and double tap the certificate. Under Details, locate Organizational Unit. This is the Team ID.
• Edit build-system/template_minimal_development_configuration.json. Use data from the previous steps.

Xcode:

• Copy and edit build-system/appstore-configuration.json.
• Generate an Xcode project:.

IPA:

• Repeat the steps from the previous section. Use distribution provisioning profiles.

Suwatte is an ad-free, open source & feature-rich comic/manga reader for iOS.

This build is distributed by a third-party not related to Suwatte.

apps.name: Nyxian
apps.subtitle: IDE to develop native code iOS apps and utilities on stock iOS it self just via a certificate and a custom micro kernel for those apps
apps.localizedDescription:
What is it?:

Nyxian is an iOS app that empowers developers with a full toolchain they can use while even being offline for iOS development on iPhone. It supports Swift, C, Objective-C, C++ and Objective-C++. It’s a powerful IDE that made the impossible possible, a fully on-device iOS IDE that doesn’t even need a cloud and can even be used with airplane mode enabled after it downloaded the SDK and resources from our server. It supports officially iOS 18.0 all the way up to the latest iOS version (iOS/iPadOS 27.2 Beta 2 tested). You can compile and run iOS apps on the go with ease, using the entire iOS 26.5 SDK.

apps.name: SceneBox
apps.subtitle: Torrent streaming client for iOS, iPadOS, tvOS and Mac (Catalyst), written in SwiftUI
apps.localizedDescription:
SceneBox:

Torrent streaming client for iOS, iPadOS, tvOS and Mac (Catalyst), written in SwiftUI.

Important:

SceneBox is a media player and BitTorrent/HTTP client. It does not provide, host, index, upload, store, or distribute any media content, and it has no affiliation with any content source.

• All catalog metadata, stream listings, and media files come from third-party services and peers that users configure or connect to. These services are independent of SceneBox, are not operated, controlled, endorsed, or reviewed by its author, and may be changed or removed at any time.

versions.localizedDescription:
Important: accounts now need your own Firebase project.

SceneBox no longer connects to a shared Firebase project. Sign-in, profiles and sync between devices now run on a free Firebase project that you create and own. Your data stays in your own account, not mine.

• Guest mode still works without any setup. Everything is kept on the device.
• To sign in, tap Connect Firebase on the sign-in screen and import the GoogleService-Info.plist from your Firebase project (on Apple TV, type in the values). Step-by-step guide and the security rules: https://github.com/donbytyqi/scenebox#firebase-setup
• Accounts made on the old shared project don't carry over. Create a new account on your own project.
• Profile photos need Firebase Storage, which requires Google's Blaze plan (it has a free tier). Everything else works on the free Spark plan.

New.

Fixes.

• Apple TV: Trakt lists open when you click them. (#10).
• Mac: signing in works on the unsigned build. macOS doesn't let unsigned apps use the Keychain, so the app keeps your sign-in session and any API keys you enter in a file inside its own sandbox container instead (readable only by your user account).

Still open.

Important: this release is NOT signed. You have to allow it yourself.

Nothing here is signed with an Apple developer account and the Mac app is not notarized. macOS and iOS will refuse to open it until you explicitly allow it. This is expected, it's not broken.

Mac:

• Open the dmg and drag SceneBox to Applications.
• Open SceneBox. macOS will say it "could not verify" the app or that it's from an unidentified developer. Press Done (not Move to Trash).
• Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll down to Security and press "Open Anyway" next to SceneBox, then confirm.
• From then on it opens normally.

If you'd rather skip the dialog, run this in Terminal after copying the app to Applications:

If you had an older signed version installed, delete it first.

iPhone/iPad: the ipa isn't signed, you sign it yourself with Sideloadly, AltStore, SideStore, Feather or ESign with your own Apple ID. Free Apple ID = resign every 7 days (AltStore/SideStore do it for you), paid dev account = one year.

Apple TV: Sideloadly works over Wi-Fi. On the TV go to Settings > Remotes and Devices > Remote App and Devices so it shows up, then pick it in Sideloadly.

apps.localizedDescription:
Halo: CE for iPhone and iPad:

Halo: Combat Evolved running natively on iPhone and iPad. It's a port of the Halo decompilation projects (see credits), compiled for ARM64 with OpenGL ES 3 graphics, SDL audio, and on-screen touch controls.

You'll need to provide your own Halo: CE XISO, which the app imports right on your device.

I've been testing it on an iPhone 17 Pro Max and an iPad Pro 13-inch (M5). The iPad imports a XISO on-device and runs at its native 2752 × 2064 resolution. It stays horizontal when turned upright. It's still early, so if you hit a bug, please open an issue.

What you need:

• An iPhone or iPad on iOS 16 or newer.

• An Apple account to sign the app.

versions.localizedDescription:
Halo: CE 0.1.2 (build 6) renders at native display resolution by default and keeps iPhone/iPad gameplay and importing in landscape.

• Retina drawable and matching internal color/depth render targets. The HUD and touch controls retain their original logical size.

• screen_width = 0 fits the display; 640 selects original 4:3 framing. See display settings.
• Landscape-only orientation masks and a full-screen orientation-lock request on recent iPadOS versions.
• In-app importing of your own original Xbox Halo XISO, the Halo: CE icon, touch controls, and hidden debug overlays remain included.

Install:

Download Halo-CE-iOS-unsigned.ipa, sign it with your own Apple account/profile, and install it. The IPA is unsigned and cannot be installed directly. Keep your existing bundle identifier when updating to retain app data. Back up the save folder before uninstalling.

Halo-CE-simulator.zip is an ARM64 simulator app for Apple Silicon Macs. The .sha256 file verifies the IPA download. See the build and installation guide.

Validation and limitations:

A signed build 6 was installed on a physical iPad Pro 13-inch (M5). Its renderer reported 2752 × 2064; the complete landscape menu was visible, and the player confirmed turning the iPad upright keeps Halo horizontal with all controls visible. All three persistent save files matched their pre-update SHA-256 hashes. The preceding build imported a real NTSC-US XISO on this iPad and reached the opening campaign scene.

Build 6 was also installed and launched on a physical iPhone 17 Pro Max. Its renderer reported 2868 × 1320, a screenshot showed the complete landscape profile menu and controls, and all three persistent save files matched their pre-update SHA-256 hashes. The earlier runtime was played with audible sound on this phone. Native-resolution campaign performance, prolonged play, older devices/OS versions, physical controllers, and multiplayer remain unverified. Anti-aliasing and an in-app graphics settings menu are not implemented yet. Bink intro videos are unsupported.

An iPadOS 27 beta simulator cold-started with a portrait canvas that cropped landscape content despite a landscape scene. This did not occur in the physical iPad session. See the validation record for coverage and remaining limitations.

Thanks to cybersecurity/halo-ce-universal, bnunu/halo-1, punpckhdq/halo, and their contributors. This product includes software developed by in. This is an unofficial community port, unaffiliated with the Halo rights holders.

apps.localizedDescription:
About:

Blinker Fluid is an experimental privacy-focused browser that ports Chromium's Blink rendering engine and V8 JavaScript engine to iOS, allowing websites to run without relying on Apple's built-in WebKit engine.

The project primarily targets jailbroken and TrollStore-capable devices, bringing a Chromium-based browser to older iOS versions where the bundled version of WebKit may struggle with some modern websites.

Why?:

I started Blinker Fluid because Ungoogled Chromium is my primary desktop browser (not counting Tor), and I wanted to see if Chromium's Blink engine could run on jailbroken iOS.

Another reason was that many modern websites no longer work correctly with older versions of WebKit bundled with older iOS releases, which many jailbroken users are unable or unwilling to update from.

Swift Radio’s stations list, Now Playing, station information and About screens have been rebuilt in SwiftUI, preserving the familiar station cards, artwork, marquee titles and popup player.

• Rebuilt navigation, popup presentation and options-sheet transitions, including returning directly to the player after sharing.

apps.localizedDescription:
TASM2 offline patch — The Amazing Spider-Man 2 (iOS 1.3.1):

Gameloft's servers for The Amazing Spider-Man 2 have been dead since ~2018, and the iOS build hangs forever on “Downloading profile”. This patches the game so it launches, plays and saves entirely offline.

Nine instructions, all in the arm64 slice, every one derived from the disassembly and verified on the binary that actually ships. No new save format, no injected code, no size change.

Confirmed on device (LiveContainer, iOS): a continuous playthrough through the prologue, all of chapter 1 and into chapter 2, with the app force-quit several times along the way. Settings, trophies, exploration, skills, position, tutorial state and the story cursor all survive.

Raw data capture ·.

First launch on macOS. NOOP is not notarized by Apple — notarization needs a paid Apple Developer ID tied to a real identity, which doesn't fit an anonymous, free project. The app is sandboxed and ad-hoc code-signed, and the full source is here to inspect. Because it isn't notarized, macOS Gatekeeper blocks it on first open (you may see "damaged" or "unverified developer" — that's the download quarantine flag, not real damage). To open it, do one of these once:

• Terminal (most reliable): drag NOOP.app to Applications, then run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/NOOP.app and open NOOP normally.

versions.localizedDescription:

Android and macOS install beside the official app; the iOS ipa carries the production bundle id, so it replaces an installed official app and uses its data. Filenames carry the base app version (v12.1.0).

• Android (debug) — NOOP-android-debug-v12.1.0.apk — debuggable build. com.noop.whoop.debug.
• macOS — NOOP-macos-v12.1.0.zip — unzip, then right-click → Open (ad-hoc signed, not notarized; Gatekeeper warns once). If it says "damaged", run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/NOOP.app.
• iOS — NOOP-ios-unsigned-v12.1.0.ipa — sideload via AltStore / Sideloadly (re-signs on-device). Replaces an installed official app (production bundle id, shared data), so back up first if you have one. apps.localizedDescription:
DreamPlayer:

DreamPlayer is a cross-platform video player for Android, iOS/iPad, and Android TV — built for true Dolby Vision, HDR10/HDR10+, and lossless audio playback.

This build is distributed by an independent third party and is not officially affiliated with the upstream DreamPlayer project.

Dolby Vision & HDR:

• True Dolby Vision playback on supported displays.
• HDR10 and HDR10+ dynamic metadata support.
• Native display headroom scaling and accurate color rendering.

Audio:

• Lossless audio decoding for all major codecs: DTS, DTS-HD, E-AC3, TrueHD, AC3, FLAC, and AAC.
• Multi-channel audio passthrough support.

Network Streaming:

• High-throughput streaming over SMB / Windows shares / NAS.
• WebDAV streaming with self-signed certificate support.
• FTP and SFTP streaming.
• Jellyfin and Emby direct playback with mDNS auto-discovery.
• UPnP and DLNA server browsing and playback.

versions.localizedDescription:
Added:

• MPV spatial audio parity with Media3 (Android 13+) — MPV now configures audiotrack and FFmpeg PCM audio before opening the file, observes MPV's actual audio-out-params, and queries Android's Spatializer through the shared system channel. The existing teal Spatial chip and info-sheet row now work in MPV mode and follow the same phone Spatial-audio setting as Media3. This supports decoded multichannel PCM from DTS/DTS-HD, TrueHD, E-AC3, AC3, FLAC, AAC, and similar tracks when the active route remains 5.1/7.1; stereo/downmixed routes and encoded bitstreams are not spatialized. MPV's audio-spdif remains intentionally unset, so this does not claim spatial processing for bitstream passthrough.
• Anime4K presets for MPV (Android) — the MPV picture panel now has an opt-in Anime4K toggle and preset selector for Mode A, B, C, A+A, B+B, and C+A. Enable the toggle first (Mode A applies by default), then selecting a preset replaces the active shader chain immediately; an Upscaled chip is shown while it is active. Only SDR MPV video is eligible: HDR/Dolby Vision and PiP reject or disable Anime4K. The bundled Anime4K v4.0.1 fast presets use legacy vo=gpu because the current shaders do not compile with vo=gpu-next/libplacebo; while enabled, libplacebo tone mapping is therefore unavailable and hardware decode may switch to mediacodec-copy. The panel warns about increased GPU load, heat, battery use, and possible stutter.
• Optional TheTVDB metadata provider — TheTVDB v4 can be configured in Settings, used as a fallback when TMDB has no confident match, or selected explicitly from Fix Match/Group Poster. Provider-qualified IDs and artwork are stored in the existing metadata cache, with TV/anime season and episode enrichment; API credentials use platform secure storage and SIMKL remains TMDB-only.

Fixed:

• TheTVDB now works on iOS (build fix) — the iOS build had been broken since TheTVDB landed, so 0.4.8 was shipped without a working TheTVDB credential store. Fixed in 0.5.0.

• Settings credential dialogs no longer overflow — the OpenSubtitles sign-in box and the TMDB API-key editor put a bare Column directly into AlertDialog.content, which overflowed the bottom of the dialog on landscape phones and at large text scales. Both now scroll like the TheTVDB dialog beside them.

• Komi-san TMDB matching — the romanized Komi-san / Komi-san wa,.

Komyushou Desu queries canonicalize to TMDB's Komi Can't Communicate, so the grouped card receives its poster and Season 1 episode titles/stills.

Pick the APK for your device and allow "Install unknown apps" when prompted:

Not sure which to pick? Grab the Universal APK.

Versioning:

apps.localizedDescription:
Photos Backup for iOS:

An experimental, fully on-device iPhone app for backing up selected photos, videos, and albums to Google Photos. It is a single SwiftUI app that completes Google account setup in an in-app web view, so everything happens on the phone without a desktop companion or hosted service.

This project uses Google's private, undocumented Photos endpoints and an Android-style authentication flow. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Google, and the integration may stop working without notice. Treat it as experimental software and use it at your own risk.

What it can do:

• Connect a Google account through Google's EmbeddedSetup flow, in an in-app web view.
• Capture the single-use oauth_token in-process from the web view's cookie store.
• Exchange the token for a Google Photos credential entirely on the device.

versions.localizedDescription:
New:

• The Google Photos app now counts what this app backs up. (, thanks @saileshbro) Uploads showed as "not backed up" in the Google Photos app, and its own Free up space never offered them. It now recognises them, and its Free up space and Delete from device remove the photos from your iPhone. On one library of about 8,500 items, "Not backed up" went from 8,145 to 0 and Free up space from 2 items to 461.The reason was the version being uploaded. The Google Photos app only counts a photo it can match to the one on your iPhone, so an edited photo or video now backs up as it looks, not as its unedited original. A photo you edited in the Google Photos app also needs the version that edit was applied on, which is uploaded in an extra step.
• Back Up Live Photo Motion. Off by default. With it on, a Live Photo's motion is attached to the still already in your account, so it plays as a Live Photo and Free up space will offer it. Live Photos backed up earlier get their motion added as a backlog — this can be tens of GB, which is why it is a setting you turn on.
• Backup keeps going after you leave the app (iOS 26). While the app is open with work to do, iOS is asked to keep it running; progress then shows in a Live Activity, where you can also stop it. Up to 2 uploads run at once in the background. On earlier iOS versions nothing changes.

Fixed:

• Google's rate limit no longer fails a row. When Google asked the app to slow down (HTTP 429), rows retried a second apart, met the same refusal, and failed. The whole queue now waits it out — a minute, doubling up to ten while Google keeps refusing — and carries on.
• Photos deleted while still queued. Freeing space on your iPhone deletes photos that may still be waiting to upload. Those rows are dropped quietly instead of failing with "no longer in your photo library" — about 2,000 rows had failed that way on one library.
• Hand-picked photos are re-checked even when the app already remembers them as backed up.

Verifying this release:

• Every pull request and every push now runs the test suite before it can land.

Worth knowing:

• An edited photo now backs up its edit, not its original. Originals already uploaded stay in your account, but a newly edited photo no longer uploads its unedited version. Google's own backup behaves the same way.
• After updating, the app queues a one-time re-check of edited photos already backed up. Most settle without uploading anything.
• A photo saved to your iPhone from Google Photos is never counted as backed up, even though it is in your library. Editing it in Apple Photos works around this.

Notes:

• 191 tests, 189 passing (2 opt-in live tests skipped).
• Tested on an iPhone 16 Pro Max (iOS 26.6.1, Google Photos 7.92.0) across a full library, and on a SideStore-signed install where the background tasks now register and run.

Unsigned IPA — install with SideStore or AltStore. Requires iOS 16+, tested on iOS 26.6. Bring your own ROM.

📖 Instrucciones en español · 🇪🇸 Notas en español abajo.

Pokémon Stadium battle models:

3D BATTLES can fight with the Pokémon Stadium models instead of the flat Game Boy pictures — STADIUM A on the map, STADIUM B on two discs against the sky.

You supply the cartridge. Import Stadium ROM in the launcher's MODS panel, or STADIUM ROM in the options menu, opens the Files picker for your Pokémon Stadium (US) 1.0 file. The models are built on your device, once, and the ROM is read and forgotten rather than kept.

That picker is new work on my side: iOS had no way to hand the mod a cartridge at all, so it printed a sandbox path and asked you to put a file somewhere a phone cannot reach. Now upstream as.

US 1.0 specifically — every model offset is measured against that revision. Another one builds, and the screen tells you the models may be wrong.

The battle HUD reads the right way round:

1.7.2 draws the battle HUD mirrored on iOS — PIKACHU, the HP numbers and L100 all backwards, while FIGHT/ITEM/RUN reads fine. It comes from a fix that assumes iOS presents the HUD canvas upside down and corrects for it; this build's renderer doesn't flip it, so the correction was the mirror. Fixed, and the frosted panels behind the HUD come back with it.

More of the mod:

• RENDER DIST — FIT / WIDE / WIDER / WIDEST / OFF. The first thing to reach for if 3D runs slowly: FIT skips whole connected maps before they cost anything.
• Fog and god rays in Viridian Forest, every battle location rebuilt, and a lot of new voxel work — diner stools, mansion desks, CUT trees.
• ROUND WORLD gained two rungs, GLOBE and PLANET. PLANET is a true half-sphere: the town sitting on a little world.

Spanish:

The Stadium screens and the whole STADIUM ROM flow are translated. Two older gaps closed: CANCEL was the one English word left on a fully Spanish options menu — structurally unreachable, now fixed and — and ten strings carried Ñ, ¿ or ¡ onto the 8×8 font, which has no glyph for any of them and drew holes instead.

The translation is.

Kept from before:

The live-tuning panel, the look stick, readable setting names, third person, the battle camera, and Spanish Red/Blue ROM support.

🇪🇸 En español:

IPA sin firmar — instalalo con SideStore o AltStore. Requiere iOS 16 o posterior; probado en iOS 26.6. Necesitas tu propia ROM.

📖 Instrucciones completas en español.

Modelos de combate de Pokemon Stadium:

COMBATES 3D puede pelear con los modelos de Pokemon Stadium en vez de con las imagenes planas de Game Boy: STADIUM A sobre el mapa, STADIUM B sobre dos discos contra el cielo.

El cartucho lo pones tu. Importar ROM de Stadium, en el panel de MODS del menu inicial, o ROM STADIUM en las opciones, abre el selector de Archivos para tu Pokemon Stadium (US) 1.0. Los modelos se crean en tu dispositivo una sola vez, y la ROM se lee y se olvida en lugar de guardarse.

Ese selector es trabajo nuevo de mi parte: en iOS no habia forma de entregarle un cartucho al mod, asi que imprimia una ruta interna y te pedia dejar un archivo en un sitio al que un telefono no llega.

US 1.0 en concreto: cada medida de los modelos esta tomada de esa revision. Otra distinta se construye igual, pero la pantalla te avisa de que pueden salir mal.

El HUD de combate se lee del derecho:

La 1.7.2 dibuja el HUD de combate reflejado en iOS: PIKACHU, los numeros de PS y L100 al reves, mientras que LUCHA/OBJETO/HUIR se lee bien. Viene de un arreglo que da por hecho que iOS presenta ese lienzo del reves y lo corrige; el motor de esta version no lo voltea, asi que la correccion era el reflejo. Arreglado, y los paneles esmerilados de detras del HUD vuelven con ello.

Mas del mod:

• DISTANCIA — AJUSTE / LEJOS / MAS LEJOS / MAXIMO / NO. Lo primero que tocar si el 3D va lento: AJUSTE descarta mapas enteros antes de que cuesten nada.
• Niebla y rayos de sol en el Bosque Verde, todas las localizaciones de combate rehechas, y mucho trabajo nuevo de voxeles.
• MUNDO CURVO gano dos niveles, GLOBO y PLANETA. PLANETA es media esfera de verdad: el pueblo sobre un planeta pequeño.

Español:

Las pantallas de Stadium y todo el proceso de ROM STADIUM estan traducidos. Se cierran dos huecos antiguos: CANCELAR era la unica palabra en ingles que quedaba en un menu de opciones completamente en español, y diez textos llevaban Ñ, ¿ o ¡ a la fuente de 8x8, que no tiene glifo para ninguno y dibujaba huecos.

Se mantiene todo lo anterior:

El panel de ajuste en vivo, la palanca de vista, los nombres legibles de los ajustes, la tercera persona, la camara de combate y el soporte de ROMs de Rojo y Azul en español.

apps.name: Solstice
apps.subtitle: Mobile variant of Horizon
apps.localizedDescription: Mobile variant of Horizon.

versions.localizedDescription:
Built on Horizon 2.4.0.

Solstice can now pull your chat log history off Horizon on your computer, exporting logs works on both platforms, and a large import no longer freezes the app.

Changes since v2026.6.4:

• Syncing copes with big log folders. Logs transfer one bounded batch at a time in both directions instead of being packed into a single archive, so neither device holds the whole log set in memory and folders that were simply too big to sync now go through. The sync screen shows progress as each batch lands, and a conversation whose stored log turns out to be damaged is reported at the end instead of quietly ending the transfer.

• A large import no longer freezes the app. Importing a desktop backup locked everything up until it finished: 16 seconds for a 58 MB backup, 85 seconds for a 296 MB one. The import now runs in small batches and gives the app room to redraw between them, so it stays responsive throughout.

• Manage Data survives signing out (#17). Its tabs no longer freeze and its dialogs open again after logging out and back in.
• Tidier sign-in screen. The checkboxes and loading spinner match the rest of the app, the stray theme name under the picker is gone, and the screen now renders in whichever theme you picked rather than only the built-in ones.
• iOS builds against the current SDK (#20). Rebuilt for the iOS 26 and Xcode 27 SDK with scene-based lifecycle support. The minimum supported version is now iOS 15.

From Horizon 2.4.0:

• Dates and times follow your language. Timestamps use your display language's formatting instead of always using English.
• Translated summaries and correct plurals. The messages shown after an export or import are translated, and counted things ("5 messages", "1 channel") use the right plural form for your language, including the missing Spanish plural in the export summary.
• Character pickers show avatars. The character select dropdowns, such as on the profile viewer and the friends dialog, show the selected character's avatar.
• Friend requests show as pending. Sending a request from the profile viewer no longer lists you as that person's friend before they have accepted.
• Channels stay grouped. The grace period for pruning grouped channels is more sensible, so channels you joined correctly are no longer ungrouped moments after connecting.
• Ads and smart filters behave. Smart filters work with "Colorize ads" off, a busy ad queue no longer lets ads slip past unfiltered, and changing a filter setting now applies to ads already on screen.
• The quick switcher respects your channel groups. It follows your group order again.
• HQ profile pictures toggle without a restart. Turning the setting on or off takes effect immediately.
• "Standardize profile fonts" no longer breaks BBCode. Profiles using characters that parse into brackets render correctly, and emoji stay visible.
• Guestbook counts are accurate. Guestbooks with more than 15 posts show the real number.
• Searching the log viewer scrolls properly. Scrolling up while searching loads older messages without having to scroll again.
• Friend colors in the All Friends tab. Names are no longer all green when you color friends and bookmarks differently.
• Accessibility fixes. Colorblind mode colors and button text contrast were corrected, and screen reader labels no longer claim every public and private channel is official.
• Species matching. Lamia and naga are no longer scored as the same species when matching profiles.

Thanks:

• @FatCatClient for cleaning up the sign-in screen (#34) and for making the login screen load non-vanilla themes (#38). Their first contributions to Solstice.
• The Horizon contributors and the Weblate translators behind everything in the section above, who keep the German, Spanish, French, Hungarian, Italian and Russian catalogs current.

versions.localizedDescription:
Theft4 0.3.2 — potential BC texture preparation fix:

Version 0.3.2 · build 144 · iPhone and iPad · 2026-10-14.

I don't have an older phone, so I cannot test these changes on one. Your mileage may vary (YMMV).

Getting “No BC textures found”? Check this first:

The first thing to check is a missing or misplaced aes_key.bin. This has now been confirmed in a 0.3.2 user log. Your game files can be present, but Theft4 needs this small file to read the texture archives. If the log says “Archive AES key is unavailable,” the app did not load the required key; this does not establish a phone/GPU problem.

Copy aes_key.bin from your validated, prepared game folder into the same folder as default.xex and default.xexp on your device. It should be named exactly aes_key.bin and be 32 bytes. Do not put it inside an extra nested folder.

If you use LiveContainer, make sure the file is in the game folder used by the copy of Theft4 inside LiveContainer.

Then close and reopen Theft4 and retry texture preparation. Version 0.3.2 will rescan after the key is restored. If it still fails, export a new log using System → Download Latest Log Capture and include your device model, iOS/app version and exact error.

What changed:

• A scan that finds zero textures is scanned again on retry instead of repeatedly reusing a failed result.
• Restoring or replacing aes_key.bin invalidates the saved source scan. Older scan identities are refreshed once; existing converted textures can still be reused by their content keys.
• Empty-scan errors now show the source-file count, resources decoded, warning count and first underlying archive/resource warning.

Update and retry:

• Update the existing app in place. Do not delete it: deletion removes its private saves and caches.
• Open Theft4, check the game files, and retry texture preparation if your GPU requires it. Allow a fresh source scan; completed conversion files remain reusable.
• Keep Theft4 open during preparation, preferably on power. Allow roughly 2.4 GB for prepared textures plus additional free working space. Pause/resume retains completed conversions.

Bug reports need logs and information:

Release v1.1.6:

• Fixed resumed manga panels not rendering until user scroll action — root cause was a desynchronization between currentPage, scrolledID, and sliderValue when restoring reading progress, which caused isAllowedToLoad to deadlock on unmounted offscreen pages.
• Fixed scrubber slider staying at page 1 on resume — slider value now initializes to the resumed page and stays synced with scroll position during normal reading.
• Improved Analytics chart scaling across long time ranges — replaced Catmull-Rom interpolation with monotone cubic to prevent negative read dips, added proper calendar units to bar marks, and implemented adaptive day/month/year bucketing for multi-year data.
• Removed dead Cache Expiry setting that was never wired to Nuke's disk cache eviction.
• Fixed inflated cache size reporting — now shows actual disk cache usage only, excluding volatile in-memory bitmap overhead.
• Stopped aggressive RAM cache purging on reader exit that was clearing all cached thumbnails app-wide.
• Cache size changes no longer rebuild the entire image pipeline — updates the existing DataCache.sizeLimit directly.

Note: I am aware of some leftover placeholder code, as well as some options that make sense in the webUI but not in the app. Unused functions exist. Broken manga detection is session-local, meaning if your connection is choppy, it could lead to false positives and might cause some mangas in the listings to disappear, this is very rare though and the benefits far outweigh any side-effects. Install:

For standalone installation, preserve com.apple.developer.kernel.increased-memory-limit=true in both Iridium's final app signature and provisioning profile. The anonymous ad-hoc carrier alone grants no installation or memory rights. In LiveContainer, the container process's signature, profile, and JIT setup determine effective rights; importing the guest IPA does not grant them. Both routes still need device validation.

Back up your saves before updating. Update the existing app or LiveContainer entry without deleting its data. iCube runs the JIT recompiler again on iOS 26. Graphics run through Vulkan on Metal via MoltenVK. Developer mode MIGHT be required on older and newer iOS, enable it going trough: Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll to the bottom, toggle on Developer Mode, and restart your device.

You need your own copy of the game. This release does not include the game's data files (textures, sounds, worlds, the original default.xex). You provide them from a disc and title update you own. This project is not affiliated with Mojang, Microsoft, or 4J Studios.

New:

• On-screen touch controls, using the layout from the XeniOS emulator. They show when no controller is connected and hide when one connects. Adjust them with touch_controls, touch_controls_opacity and touch_haptics in mc360.toml.
• Save thumbnails: your worlds now show a picture in the world list.
• Exit Game now closes the app instead of leaving a black screen.

Performance:

• Much lower CPU load while playing. The game's threads no longer queue up on a shared lock, calls inside the game run directly, and waits end as soon as the GPU is ready instead of sleeping in whole milliseconds.
• Frame rate capped at a steady, evenly paced 60 FPS (framerate_limit, default 60).
• The game's main thread and GPU thread now get priority on the iPhone's performance cores.
• Less heat: the game no longer spins a core at full power while waiting for the GPU, and no longer copies the whole screen image back and forth several times per frame.

Fixes:

• Fixed random crashes after playing for a while.
• Fixed choppy audio.
• Fixed "ghost" blocks and old terrain showing where the world had changed.
• Devices with 3 GB of RAM now show an explanation at launch instead of crashing.

Known issues:

• Long sessions heat the phone, and iOS then slows it down, so the frame rate can drop over time. Playing unplugged and without a case helps.
• The on-screen D-pad's up arrow sits over the first world's thumbnail in the Load menu. It's part of the controls, not the save.
• Devices with 3 GB of RAM (iPhone 8 Plus, iPhone X, iPad 8th gen) can't run the game with a normal sideload. They need TrollStore, or a signing method that grants the Extended Virtual Addressing entitlement.

Installing over 1.0 keeps your worlds and settings.

versions.localizedDescription:
ByeTunes v2.6 – Favorites, Playlist Pinning & Background Downloads Reworked:

Hi guys, here is the 2.6 update for ByeTunes. A good amount of things got added, fixed and improved in this one. You can now properly favorite injected songs, pin playlists from inside ByeTunes, and keep downloads going in the background with a new Picture in Picture window. There were also a bunch of fixes around metadata, library management and database safety.

Favorites.

There are three new options inside Library Repair:

• Create Favorites Playlist creates the Favorites playlist using the right name for your device region.
• Fix Missing Favorites repairs songs injected with an older version that you already favorited but that never actually appeared in Favorites.
• Delete Favorites Playlist lets you delete that playlist from Library Repair.

Songs injected from 2.6 onwards now get their store IDs during injection, so you can favorite them right away. If the metadata fetcher finds a match, ByeTunes uses the IDs from that match. Songs without a match get generated IDs instead.

Quick recommendation: if you have older injected songs that you favorited but cannot find in Favorites, run Fix Missing Favorites inside Library Repair.

Playlist Pinning.

You can now pin and unpin playlists from the On-Device Library. Long-press a playlist or use the Pin button from inside it.

Keep in mind: pinning and unpinning these playlists needs to be done through ByeTunes. The Pin option inside the Apple Music app does not work for them.

Background Downloads.

Background downloads got a big rework. ByeTunes now uses silent audio to keep downloads going in the background, with an optional Picture in Picture window so you can see what is happening after leaving the app.

The window shows the current song's progress, what is next in the queue, and when metadata is being fetched. You can also customize it with themes, your own colors or a background picture. There is a live preview in Settings so you can see how it looks before using it.

This replaces the old background download behavior and Live Activity support. Download progress now shows in the Picture in Picture window.

If the app closes while songs are still downloading, those songs go back to the front of the queue the next time you open ByeTunes.

Pause and Cancel were fixed too. They now properly stop background transfers instead of accidentally starting a fallback download after you already paused or cancelled the song.

Download Queue & Saving Files.

Downloaded songs now get their metadata as part of the download process. You will see a "fetching metadata" state before the song is marked as done, instead of that work being left to a separate background metadata manager.

A few other things got added or improved:

• Clear All for completed items in the queue sheet.
• Preview buttons in the album sheet and artist profile.

• A new Save With Fetched Metadata toggle that writes the fetched tags and cover artwork into the MP3 and FLAC copies you save.

Metadata Fixes.

Metadata matching got a lot of attention in this update. There were cases where a remix could get the original song's information, or a song could get renamed to a different track from the same album. Those issues should now be fixed.

• Apple Music track matching now checks the title, so songs should no longer get relabeled as another track from that album.
• Apple Music search pages are requested in English so ByeTunes can find the Songs and Albums sections even when using a non-English storefront.
• A Deezer result with missing artwork or an unreadable item no longer causes the entire search to come back empty.

FLAC handling was improved too. Some changes in the downloaded files were causing every song to take the album name as its title when an ALBUMTITLE tag was present. That is fixed now.

Album artist is also read correctly from files using the ALBUM ARTIST or album_artist tags.

Library Management.

Added sorting, a genre filter and multi-delete to the Library management tab.

Fixed an issue where the library would only show some of your songs, for example just 50 tracks. ByeTunes was only scanning one folder. It now scans all folders so the rest of your songs show up too.

Injected songs now use the file's creation date for a more accurate date.

Deleting songs also cleans up any albums, artists and artwork entries left empty after the deletion.

Stability, Backups & Database Safety.

There were also several fixes to make injection, transfers and backups more reliable:

• One unreadable local file no longer stops the whole injection batch.
• The export folder is checked before transferring files. If it cannot be used, ByeTunes falls back to its own Exports folder.
• Snapshot backups keep the previous snapshot until the new one finishes successfully, and only replace snapshots of the same kind.
• The heartbeat timeout handles stale connection attempts more reliably.

Overall stability and database safety were improved too.

Cleanup.

The old background metadata manager and its pending import pipeline were removed, since downloaded songs now get their metadata directly during the download process.

The Live Activity extension and download tracking were also removed as part of the move to Picture in Picture, along with the old background download behavior and unused code.

Official Backend & Building Your Own.

I also added BACKEND_TERMS.md, which explains how the official hosted backend may be used. Modified builds need to use their own backend.

If you are building ByeTunes yourself, Config.example.plist is now included as a template for the backend address. The README explains how to set it up.

I also reorganized the project structure. Files are now grouped into proper folders so everything is easier to find and work on. This should help anyone working on their own fork of ByeTunes understand where things are and make changes more easily. I am also considering a bigger rewrite of the app down the road, so this cleanup is a step towards that, but nothing is confirmed yet.

Thanks as always to everyone testing ByeTunes, sending logs and reporting what breaks. Hope you guys enjoy this update.

apps.localizedDescription:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec24f92e-d29a-4319-8293-439487d60b35

Features:

• Native Engine: Runs flawlessly on iOS, due to the official PICO-8 engine being implemented as a WASM module.
• Quick Save & Load: The only PICO-8 experience with instant save states. Freeze time and resume anywhere, across devices.

• Adaptive Controls: Custom Gameboy-esque controls with tactile haptics. Works in portrait and landscape. Swap to virtual joystick.

Technical Look:

The core engineering challenge was reconciling the asynchronous nature of mobile file I/O with the synchronous requirements of the Emscripten/WASM virtual file system.

PICO-8 demands a synchronous file system. Bridging this to mobile required completely reverse-engineering the Emscripten boot sequence.

Runs at a locked 60fps on an iPhone 13 mini (A15): median frame 16.7ms against a 16.67ms budget, 95th percentile 16.8-17.8ms. Anything newer has more headroom than that.

Step 3 is the whole thing: it checks your tools, extracts your disc image, recompiles it, builds the app, signs it with your Apple ID, and installs it on your phone.

--recurse-submodules matters - the runtime lives in a submodule and the build will not configure without it. If you already cloned without it, run git submodule update --init --recursive inside skate3recomp-dev.

versions.localizedDescription:
Skate 3 Recompiled v2.7.1 — iOS:

iOS skipped a release. Everything Android got in v0.2.0 is here, plus two iOS-specific defaults. 24 engine commits and 17 SDK commits since v2.6.3.

Put any button anywhere:

Full controller remapping, on the Controls page under Button Mapping. Sixteen inputs — the four face buttons, both bumpers, both triggers, both stick clicks, Back, Start and the four D-pad directions — can each be moved to any of the others. Your mapping is saved and survives an update.

The sticks themselves are not remapped; Swap Sticks and Invert Camera Y already cover that.

Three bugs that were costing you frames:

Touching the frame-rate row uncapped the game. One setting's name was a prefix of another's (._fps_cap inside ._fps_cap_auto), so changing the Framerate Cap row erased the shipped cap entirely, on every launch after you touched that row. The game then ran the guest loop uncapped. On Android that also meant rendering roughly twice the frames the panel could show and dumping the rest as heat, which is what "runs at 60, drops after a few minutes" was there; iOS presents through FIFO, so the cost here is wasted work rather than heat.

"The frame rate is fine but it feels like slow motion." Skate 3 advances exactly one refresh period of simulation per rendered frame, however long that frame took, so a 33 ms frame runs the game at half speed. The ceiling that lets a frame advance more than one period (skate3_frame_advance_cap) had been compiled for Switch only — iOS and Android, the two platforms whose frames overrun the period most, never got it. It is compiled in on iOS now.

Being straight about this one: the clamp is in and reachable, but raising it was measured as changing nothing on hardware, so treat it as a lever that now exists rather than a fix you are guaranteed to feel.

A profiler was running in every build. A per-packet GPU timer took two clock reads and two atomic increments on every command packet — around 1.7 million clock reads a second on the busiest thread — whether or not anyone was profiling. It is off unless you ask for it.

First launch could come up blank:

Roughly one clean install in ten reached the setup screen with an empty options list and no way forward. Parts of a screen drawn once while their shaders were still compiling were skipped and never came back — and the difficulty prompt is drawn exactly once. Shader compilation now stays synchronous through the cold-boot frontend, so nothing can draw before it is ready.

Eleven new rows, most of them aimed at buying frames back on a phone:

• 3D Scene Resolution — Full / 75% / 67% / 50% / 40%, separate from UI sharpness.
• Draw Distance — now goes down to Quarter and Eighth.
• NPC Update Rate and World Update Rate.
• Pedestrians & Traffic, Movable Props, Other Skaters — stop the world spawning crowds you are not looking at (all three need a restart).
• Vegetation, Hair Detail, Water Effects, Draw Batching.
• Framerate Cap — 40, 45 and 50 added (40 divides 120 Hz, 45 divides 90 Hz).
• FPS Percentiles — the 1% low and p95/p99 next to the average (darchap's, see Credit).

Known limitation on the three population cuts: they remove the bodies, not the gameplay objects behind them, so you may still hear pedestrians, traffic and other skaters you cannot see. Being worked on. The average is exactly the statistic that hides a stutter: a steady 60 and a 60 that drops four frames a second read the same.

Two changed defaults on iOS:

• Draw distance now ships at Half. The static world is roughly 750 of the 765 things drawn in a frame, so it is the only content lever with real weight behind it. The trade is real: props, street furniture and foliage pop in closer than they did in 2.6.3. Settings > Video > Draw Distance > Original puts it back.This applies to new installs only. If you are updating, your existing draw distance is kept exactly as it is — the game records your video settings the first time it runs, and a new default never overwrites settings that are already on your device. To get the new one, set the row to Half yourself.
• FPS Percentiles ships on, so the 1% low is there as soon as you turn the FPS counter on. The counter itself is still off by default.

Under the hood:

• The render pass stays open when the target has not changed.
• The tonemap and HUD passes can be merged into one (off by default).
• The guest is parked while the app is in the background, instead of running on against a surface that is gone.
• The texture budget is enforced between rescans.
• Shader compilation stays synchronous through the cold-boot frontend, so the first-run setup screen cannot draw before its shaders exist.

Installing:

Bring your own copy of the game — no game content ships in this IPA. See the README for the ISO and title-update steps.

Credit:

This is a packaging of other people's work as much as my own.

• Alex McHugh — skate3recomp. The Skate 3 recompilation itself. None of this exists without it.
• portingpete — skate3-recomp. Early bring-up on ReXGlue.

• Buku313 — Skate3-Mobile. A parallel ARM64 port; the 16 KB page-alignment fix came from there.
• ReXGlue SDK and Xenia (Ben Vanik and contributors) underneath it all.

apps.name: Husk
apps.subtitle: Run Android on iOS. Natively or Emulated
apps.localizedDescription:
Husk:

Android apps and games on your iPhone.

Add an APK, tap it, and it opens full-screen. Husk runs it in one of two ways, shown as the two sides of its Library:

• Translation Layer. The game's own 64-bit Android code runs directly on the iPhone's processor, and Husk stands in for Android around it: the C library, the Java calls the game makes, OpenGL ES (through ANGLE), Vulkan (through MoltenVK), sound, touch and controllers. No Android boots, so a game starts in seconds, and its code is never emulated.
• Emulation. A full Android system (LineageOS) boots under QEMU inside Husk, for apps the translation layer cannot run yet and for using Android itself. iOS gives apps no hypervisor, so the processor is emulated, and this is much slower than the translation layer.

iPhone & iPad:

• Game speed holds real time under load — races no longer slow down when the frame rate dips.
• Jumbotron / TV screens no longer stall the GPU every frame.

Play The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask on your iPhone and Apple Vision Pro — the full three-day cycle with saves, the 2 Ship 2 Harkinian enhancements menu, HD/4K texture packs, game controllers and a tunable touch layout, and on Vision Pro a stereoscopic 3D mode that puts the game on a world-locked panel floating in your room with real depth.

versions.localizedDescription:
A performance and controls update for iPhone, plus a launch-crash fix. Your saves and extracted mm.o2r carry over unchanged; no re-extraction needed.

iPhone & iPad.

• Smoother and faster: holds a locked 120 fps on a 120 Hz iPhone with an HD texture pack. Music no longer slows down when frames run late, because the game clock keeps real time. • Launch-crash fix: if your settings had the renderer set to OpenGL (which this app does not include), the game crashed at launch. It now falls back to Metal and repairs the setting by itself. Settings > Graphics > Renderer API lists Metal only.
• Drag-to-look: with Free Look on, swipe on empty screen space to move the camera (sensitivity slider in the iOS settings). Holding a touch C-button no longer swings the camera.
• Gyro aiming (off by default, with a sensitivity slider): tilt the phone to aim the bow, hookshot and first-person view.
• Always Show Menu Button: a new option that keeps the menu button on screen during gameplay.
• iOS settings section restored: 1.1.0 and 1.1.1 accidentally shipped a cut-down version of it. Double-Tap Z, Haptics, Opacity, Left-Handed, Stick Response, Customize Layout, Max Frame Rate, Supersampling and the Performance HUD are back in the menu.
• The touch R button now acts as the right trigger.
• Built with the iOS 27 SDK: launches correctly and stays landscape on iOS 27.

Apple Vision Pro.

Logging in may break at random due to Apple's constant server-side changes. If login fails, make sure that you're on the latest version of PancakeStore. Do NOT open any issues or ask for support regading logins. It will not speed up the process of fixing authentication.

Before you continue...:

• Not only is authentication unstable, but there is no guarantee that user data will be retained when downgrading! Use this tool at your own risk.

versions.localizedDescription:
EoL Notice:

PancakeStore is officially EoL (End-of-Life) as of 8/22/2026.

Apple has implemented server-side changes to the iTunes API that's used in PancakeStore, as well as other popular tools such as ipatool, which primarily include SEP-based device attestation. What this means, in short, is that PancakeStore will not work ever again unless someone figures out an alternative route for downgrading apps, or successfully re-implements the attestation logic (both of which are very difficult).

In the event that this occurs, or a new method for downgrading apps is discovered and made, we will update PancakeStore. Until then, consider the project EoL.

Thank you all for all of your support of this tool, and we apologize that things have to halt like this.

❤️.

As you can see, lots more languages compared to just over a day ago. We are very thankful for all of our volunteer translators for their contributions and assistance.

apps.name: SkyStream
apps.subtitle: SkyStream is a modern, cross-platform media streaming client inspired by CloudStream. It uses a custom JavaScript runtime for plugins, allowing users to scrape and stream content from various sources on Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, and Linux from a single codebase
apps.localizedDescription:
SkyStream:

⚠️ Warning: By default, this app doesn't provide any video sources; you have to install extensions to add functionality to the app.

A new, cross-platform media streaming application inspired by CloudStream.

Note: This project is an independent application built with Flutter. While it supports similar extension formats, it is a simplified, modern re-imagining and is not a direct clone or fork of the official client.

Please don't create illegal extensions or use any that host any copyrighted media. This project does not condone copyright infringement.

Overview:

SkyStream is a modern, media streaming client. It draws inspiration from the versatile architecture of CloudStream but implements a custom, cross-platform JavaScript engine for extensions, enabling support for Android, iOS, and Desktop from a single codebase.

versions.localizedDescription:
🧩 CloudStream Extensions:

• CloudStream (.cs3) extensions on every platform – Install and run CloudStream extensions on Android, iOS, macOS, Windows and Linux. Their providers appear on Home, in search and in the provider list.
• Repositories – Add a repository by its URL (repo.json or plugins.json), a cloudstreamrepo:// link or a shortcode. MegaRepo is supported, Check Updates shows what changed, and each extension can be updated or removed.
• Extension settings – An extension's own settings open in SkyStream on every platform and take effect without restarting the app. Extensions' own dialogs and pages open in SkyStream too.
• Full-screen extension windows – Extensions that open a full-screen page, games included, work on every platform, and Back closes them.
• One switch – Turn CloudStream off entirely in Settings: no extension loads and their providers are hidden everywhere. Nothing is uninstalled.
• Richer details – A CloudStream title's page shows everything its extension provides: its logo, score, content rating, status and tags; cast with voice actors; trailers; more titles from the same extension; when the next episode airs; named seasons; and each episode's rating, runtime and air date. A title not out yet says Coming soon. Tracking and skip times now get the title's MAL, AniList, IMDb and TMDB ids.

🛡️ Bot Checks (Cloudflare and Others):

• SkyStream's own browser engine – Bot checks are now cleared in each platform's own browser engine on every platform, Linux included, instead of the old WebView plugin.
• Checks cleared for you – SkyStream ticks the checkbox itself where it can. When a site needs you, its check opens right where you are.
• One check per site – A site cleared once works for SkyStream plugins, CloudStream extensions, Nuvio scrapers and Stremio add-ons alike, and stays cleared across restarts until the site asks again.
• See each site's check – Search, Explore and Home show the sites that need a check, with Verify for one site or all of them. A site can be set not to open its check by itself.
• Clearer reasons – A site that blocks VPNs, keeps asking, can't be reached, or needs a newer Android System WebView says so.
• Moved sites followed – When a site moves to a new address, SkyStream follows it.
• More check vendors – DDoS-Guard and other vendors are handled, and a captcha an extension asks for is shown to you to solve.

🔎 Search:

• Universal search – One search bar for SkyStream, CloudStream, Stremio and Nuvio: a section for each Stremio add-on and one for Nuvio, with every result tagged with where it came from.
• Search in every language – Titles are found whatever their accents, letter forms, digits or spacing: "pokemon" finds "Pokémon", and Arabic, Persian, Urdu, Hebrew, Turkish and Indian-language titles match the way they are typed. Japanese, Chinese and Thai titles written without spaces are found by any part of the name, and Korean ones with or without spaces. A provider whose titles are all in another script shows them instead of nothing (PR #127).
• Traditional and Simplified Chinese – A search in either finds titles written in the other: 复仇者联盟 finds 復仇者聯盟, and 活着 finds 活著.

🎬 Player & Playback:

• Volume and brightness swipes like VLC – Both follow your finger with no lag. The volume boost above 100% shows in orange, and a swipe from below 100% stops there first: swipe up again to go past it.
• Volume keys – On Android the volume keys change the video's volume even while it is paused. On a desktop keyboard, holding a volume key keeps stepping.
• Orientation – Leaving the player returns to your device's orientation, with the rotation lock respected.
• Rotate button – On phones and tablets, a Rotate button turns the player between landscape and portrait. The player still turns to fit each video first; your choice holds for the rest of that video, and the next one fits itself again. It can be hidden in Player Controls. iPads and Android 16 tablets don't let apps turn the screen, so they don't have it.
• Faster playback – Playback speed now goes up to 4x, with 3x and 4x among the quick choices.
• New player controls – Frosted controls, and one Options button for sources, audio, subtitles and episodes. The volume and episode buttons can be hidden in Player Controls (PR #121).
• Held keys – Holding left or right on a keyboard or a TV remote, or J/L on a keyboard, keeps seeking (PR #121).
• Audio language – Choose the language videos start in, in Player settings. A video with an audio track in that language starts on it, including after a source change and on the next episode; one without it plays its own default. A track you pick from Audio in the player stays for the rest of that video (PR #130).
• More languages – Persian, Filipino, Thai and Azerbaijani can be chosen as the audio language and in subtitle search, and SubSource now finds Chinese subtitles.
• Subtitles from Stremio add-ons – The player's subtitle search also asks your Stremio subtitle add-ons, and OpenSubtitles' own Stremio add-on, so a film or an episode with an IMDb id finds subtitles with no key or account.
• Subtitle style in the player – A Subtitle style page in the player's Subtitles tab sets the size, colours, background, outline, position, bold, font, text opacity and encoding, on every device including TV; Settings has the same choices. Subtitle files change at once. Subtitles inside the video change from their next line, and take bold, font, text opacity and encoding the next time the player opens (PR #133).
• Play Stremio titles from their page – When the add-on a title came from also brings its links, as CNCVerse Bridge does, the title's page has a Play button (Resume once started, and the next episode for a show), its episodes are laid out like a CloudStream title's and play with a tap, and the player goes on to the next episode from the same add-on. Holding an episode searches every add-on for it, as Search Stremio add-ons does.
• Choose a stream's quality – A stream that offers several qualities (HLS) gets a Quality tab in the player's Options: Auto, or any quality it offers, with every audio track kept. Your choice holds for the rest of that viewing, through source changes and the next episodes. Auto now follows your Wi-Fi & Wired and Mobile quality preferences, and such streams are listed at your preferred quality instead of last.
• Videos start sooner – A video starts once a second of it has loaded, instead of three: MP4 files start about a second sooner.
• Read-ahead sized for each video – The player reads about three minutes ahead (one on mobile data, six for very high-bitrate files), worked out from the video's bitrate, and never more than this device's memory allows. Network buffer in Player settings now offers Auto (recommended), which everyone starts on, or a fixed size.
• Fewer stalls on a weak connection – On HLS streams, Auto quality steps down before the video runs out, not after.
• Live streams closer to live, with a rewind – Live streams start closer to the live edge. On a live stream that keeps the last minutes, the progress bar covers them: step or drag back to catch what you missed, see how far behind live you are, and tap LIVE to catch up.
• One buffering spinner, everywhere – It shows when the picture freezes, never while you drag the progress bar, and goes the moment the video moves again.
• Streams come back by themselves – When the connection drops, the server stalls or the network goes, the last picture stays on screen with "Reconnecting…" or "Waiting for network…", and playback picks up where it stopped as soon as the stream is back. A source is only given up on when its server says it's gone, or another source's server answers while this one stays silent.
• Slow starts get their time – A stream that is still loading isn't abandoned at 30 seconds; one that shows no sign of life is.
• Torrents start on the right buffer – TorrServer now gets the buffer size SkyStream chooses for each film, instead of running on its 64 MB default, and the film is no longer held twice in memory. While a torrent prepares, the screen shows its peers, speed and how much is loaded.
• Season packs play the episode you picked from Stremio add-ons, instead of the pack's first file.

🖥️ Interface:

• Navigation bar – A new frosted navigation bar on phones (PR #121).

🔐 Accounts:

• MyAnimeList and AniList sign-in inside SkyStream – Signing in happens in the app, on every platform.
• Trakt's new sign-in – Trakt now signs in through Trakt's new sign-in page. If you were signed in to Trakt before, you may be asked to connect once more.
• Simkl's new sign-in – Connecting Simkl now uses Simkl's new sign-in (AUTH V2), the same code to enter on simkl.com/pin. Simkl retires the old one around April 2027; if you're already connected, you stay connected.

🐞 Bug Fixes & System Stability:

• 🛠️ Fixed: switching audio or subtitles paused the video to rebuffer – A switch now changes only the track, and the new audio plays within about a second.
• 🛠️ Fixed: seeks in HLS streams could be lost – A seek, or resuming where you left off, sometimes never happened. It now lands.
• 🛠️ Fixed: some Android devices were taken for low-memory ones – SkyStream read whether memory was short at that moment, not the device's own low-memory flag, and held such devices to a lower video quality.

• 🛠️ Fixed: some streams had no Quality tab on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Windows and Linux – Streams SkyStream relays for their headers now offer it like any other.
• 🛠️ Fixed: on Windows, the first video after starting the app took long to open – The player's components are now indexed once, when SkyStream is installed or first run.
• 🛠️ Fixed: seeking in some HLS streams with subtitles took seconds longer (iPhone, iPad, Mac, Windows and Linux) – A seek the player turns down is now sent again at once.
• 🛠️ Fixed: on Android, the first video after installing SkyStream was slow to start – The player now builds its list of fonts in the background as soon as SkyStream first starts, instead of when that video opens.
• 🛠️ Fixed: on Android, video could play with sound but no picture after the player reopened a stream.
• 🛠️ Fixed: on Mac, a dropped connection paused the video, and a film's end paused instead of showing the end card.
• 🛠️ Fixed: on iPhone, iPad and Mac, switching streams quickly could crash or freeze the app.

• 🛠️ Fixed: the "None of the sources would play" screen kept the display awake – It now lets the screen sleep, and Retry keeps it awake again.
• 🛠️ Fixed: on phones, a video still loading when you left the app started playing in the background.
• 🛠️ Fixed: the buffering spinner flickered on some streams while they played fine.
• 🛠️ Fixed: HDR streams were ranked above others, though SkyStream shows HDR washed out.
• 🛠️ Fixed: the audio and subtitle lists blinked and moved the remote's cursor while open on some streams – The rows stay put, with the cursor where you left it.
• 🛠️ Fixed: a page in a sign-in or bot-check sheet couldn't be scrolled on phones – On Android and iPhone the page scrolls under your finger, and the sheet moves by its handle only. Sheets, Home's long-press menus and the source list for an external player now open above the navigation bar instead of under it.
• 🛠️ Fixed: lines from a subtitle file flickered – They no longer blink off and on or flash an earlier line, worst on HLS streams, and a short seek back shows the line it lands in (PR #132).
• 🛠️ Fixed: posters didn't show for some sites behind a bot check – Once SkyStream has cleared a site's check, its posters and artwork load too.
• 🛠️ Fixed: SubSource found no subtitles without an API key – SubSource retired the way SkyStream searched it without a key. It is now searched the way subsource.net searches itself, with no key needed, and a key works as before.
• 🛠️ Fixed: OpenSubtitles found no Chinese or Portuguese subtitles – Simplified, Traditional and bilingual Chinese, and Brazil's and Portugal's Portuguese are found now, and OpenSubtitles VIP accounts use their own server.

• 🛠️ Fixed: some subtitles from Stremio add-ons showed a code instead of their language – They show the language's name, and Traditional Chinese, Spain's Spanish and Kurdish ones are picked for a viewer who reads them.
• 🛠️ Fixed: on TV, the remote could end up behind the player's open panel – When playback reopened its source while the panel was open, after a quality change, a source failing over or the network coming back, the remote moved to the controls behind it.
• 🛠️ Fixed: some repository short links and shortcodes didn't add their repository – Links that pass through a redirect page now work, a shortcode works in any letter case ("Universe" adds SkyStream's own collection), and the add-repository boxes no longer autocorrect what you type (PR #129).
• 🛠️ Fixed: another repository could replace an extension with its own code – An extension now updates only from the repository it was installed from, and only to the extension that repository lists. To move an extension to another repository, use Install from this repository in that repository's list.
• 🛠️ Fixed: on TV, a keyboard closed with Back couldn't be opened again from its text field – OK on the field opens it again, and Down moves on from the field to what is below it, in search on Home, Explore and the Search tab and in the text boxes of dialogs (PR #128).
• 🛠️ Fixed: on some low-memory Google TV devices, the on-screen keyboard showed but typed nothing into SkyStream.
• 🛠️ Fixed: on iPad, a video's sound stopped a second in – The video went on playing silently until an audio track was picked again.
• 🛠️ Fixed: leaving the player could freeze the app on iPad.
• 🛠️ Fixed: brightness swipes lagged on iPhone and iPad – The brightness changed only after the finger stopped.
• 🛠️ Fixed: on iPad and Android tablets, a tapped icon in the side navigation bar stayed enlarged – It grew and showed its label as if a mouse were over it. The bar now grows only under a mouse, or for a remote or keyboard.
• 🛠️ Fixed: the app could open in landscape after leaving the player.
• 🛠️ Fixed: on Linux, the screen stopped going to sleep after playback until SkyStream was closed.
• 🛠️ Fixed: on Linux, opening some streams, such as Internet Archive's, froze the app.
• 🛠️ Fixed: on TV, the search screen's scope selector and first result ignored the D-pad.
• 🛠️ Fixed: Continue Watching couldn't reopen Stremio titles – Tapping one, or View Details on a long press, opened a plugin's page that couldn't load it. It now opens the title's own page, through the add-on it came from; a title started before this update does so once it's played again.
• 🛠️ Fixed: Stremio shows that an add-on publishes as "other" were treated as films – CNCVerse Bridge publishes its shows that way. Their episodes now keep their own progress and watched marks, and their page calls them a series.
• 🛠️ Fixed: on TV, Left could jump up to the top of a page instead of into the side navigation bar – From a button with nothing beside it, such as Select Provider on Home, Left went to the arrows at the top. It now opens the side navigation bar.
• 🛠️ Fixed: on Windows, macOS and Linux, Clear cache could delete other apps' temporary files – It now clears only SkyStream's own.
• 🛠️ Fixed: the Linux .deb didn't install the VLC and WebKitGTK it needs – apt now installs them with SkyStream.
• 🛠️ Fixed: the Linux x64 build didn't start on Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12 and other systems older than Ubuntu 24.04 (PR #121).

⚙️ Improvements:

• 🚀 Linux AppImage for x64 and arm64, beside the .deb and the archive (PR #125).
• 🚀 For repository authors: a SkyStream repository lists its plugins in pluginLists files; a plugins list inside the repository's own manifest is no longer read.
• 🚀 Updated to Flutter 3.47.7, Android Gradle Plugin 9.1.1 and VLC 3.0.24.
• 🚀 Fewer third-party plugins: flutter_inappwebview, screen_brightness and flutter_volume_controller are gone, replaced by SkyStream's own.
• 🚀 Thousands of new automated tests, and checks that run the app on every platform.

About:

Roam Control is an iPhone app for location-based development, quality assurance and responsible personal testing on a device you own and control.

It supports fixed reported locations, Walking, Driving and Cycling routes, Joystick movement, GPX import/export, favourites, history, on-device pairing and guided LocalDevVPN-compatible sessions.

Roam Control is distributed as a prebuilt IPA. The application source code is not publicly distributed.

Features:

• Search for places, enter coordinates or select a position on the map.
• Start and update a fixed reported location.
• Simulate Apple Maps Walking, Driving and Cycling routes.
• Build manual routes with point-by-point or freehand drawing.
• Import and export GPX routes.
• Move freely with the Joystick without creating a route.
• Pause, resume, reverse or redirect active route sessions.

versions.localizedDescription:
Stability and reliability improvements:

Roam Control 0.9.7 is a maintenance update focused on background location-session reliability and mobile-data connectivity.

What's improved:

• Improved native connection handling for LocalDevVPN.
• Corrected network-interface selection when LocalDevVPN and a separate Personal VPN are active simultaneously.
• Improved reliability in tested background and mobile-data scenarios.
• Verified fixed locations, Walking, Driving, Cycling, Stop & Restore and LocalDevVPN reconnection.

These improvements were validated on the developer's iPhone. Compatibility with every VPN configuration is not guaranteed.

No new features, interface changes or pairing implementation changes.

Installation:

Requires iOS 27 or later, Developer Mode and LocalDevVPN.

The IPA is unsigned and can be signed using SideStore.

Upgrading directly from 0.9.4? Back up your favourites, history and supported settings before installing. The app identifier changed in 0.9.5, so existing data will not automatically transfer. Pairing must be completed again.

Install:

apps.localizedDescription:
Kryptos:

Kryptos is an iOS and Android application that allows you to encrypt messages in regular messengers. It also works with messengers where end-to-end encryption is not enabled by default, including Telegram, Instagram, WeChat, as well as regular SMS.

You can write a message in any messenger and encrypt it using the “lock” button on the Kryptos keyboard. The ciphertext will appear in the messenger’s input field and can be sent as a regular message.

On Android, Kryptos can decrypt a message directly in the messenger’s chat, so you do not need to constantly open Kryptos to decrypt messages. On iPhone, the decrypted text is automatically displayed in the keyboard after copying the ciphertext.

Kryptos uses the same ciphertext format on both platforms, so the sender and recipient can use different operating systems.

apps.subtitle: Run x86-64 Windows PC games on jailed iOS via FEX-Emu + Wine + DXMT
apps.localizedDescription:
Madeira runs Windows PC games on an iPhone, with no jailbreak. Games run as they are, unmodified, inside a single iOS app.

Madeira is an active research project. Many games start and some play well, but performance and compatibility vary from game to game, and things change quickly. Expect rough edges.

How it works:

iOS apps cannot start other programs, so everything runs in one process: even Wine's server runs as a thread instead of a separate program.

Features:

• Game library with artwork, search and a Windows desktop session.

versions.localizedDescription:
New:

• In-app JIT: no StikDebug needed. Madeira can enable JIT by itself through a bundled helper built on StikJIT. On iOS 27 it pairs with the iPhone it runs on: in Settings › Privacy & Security › Developer Mode, tap Pair with Madeira and enter the PIN Madeira shows. No computer needed. On iOS 26, import a pairing file instead. The pairing is kept in the Keychain. StikDebug still works. (#127).
• Play turns JIT on for you. If JIT is off, Play enables it and then starts the game. The button reads Starting JIT meanwhile.
• Madeira JIT shortcut (iOS 27, optional). LocalDevVPN's loopback does not work over cellular data. The shortcut connects LocalDevVPN, turns Cellular Data off when there is no Wi-Fi, and puts both back once the game has started, along with any VPN you were using. Add it during setup or in Settings › JIT.
• Steam Cloud saves for installed Steam games, on by default. Saves sync before and after you play, and the cloud copy is backed up before it is replaced. (#130).
• A controller as keyboard and mouse, chosen per game, with a Controller binds page. DirectInput is now a per-game choice too. (#128).
• Setup starts by installing LocalDevVPN when it is missing. It opens once more after this update, so you can pick one of the new JIT options.

Fixed:

• Games start faster: Wine starts as soon as the wineserver is ready, not after a fixed 2 s. (#125).
• Cuphead (#107), Nine Sols (#108) and Hades II (#119, #120) now run, and Steam app info with escaped quotes is read correctly (#118).
• JIT errors now explain the problem and offer a fix: Pair Again or Connect LocalDevVPN. The error also shows on the Settings tab.

Known issues:

• With Wi-Fi and Cellular Data both off, LocalDevVPN cannot connect, so JIT cannot be enabled, even with the shortcut. Connect LocalDevVPN while a network is available.

Install:

• Requires iOS 26 or later. In-app pairing and the Madeira JIT shortcut need iOS 27.
• If your sideloader asks whether to keep app extensions, keep them: Madeira's in-app JIT runs in one.
• The IPA is ad-hoc signed (no certificate) and carries the app's entitlements, including the increased memory limit. Sideload it with your own Apple ID (SideStore, AltStore, Sideloadly, Plume or similar), which signs it for your device.
• First-run setup walks you through JIT. Settings shows JIT and Memory+ with green checks and says Ready to play.

Not included:

The Microsoft Visual C++ runtime DLLs are not redistributed (see legal/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md). Building from source: tools/fetch-vcruntime.md.

Thanks to Dan Perks (@danperks) for in-app JIT and pairing, Jesse (@JesseLovelace) for Steam Cloud saves, faster launches and the game fixes, and Nick (@125hz) for keyboard-and-mouse controllers.

versions.localizedDescription:
VortX 0.5.5: Lighter Sync, Hero Trailers and Your Next Episode:

Build 274. VortX 0.5.5 fixes repeated conversion of unchanged 0.4 account data and reduces unnecessary background polling while live sync is healthy. These changes address a source of lag, stutter and delayed taps across the Apple apps. Hero trailers start again, Mac and iPad series pages open on your episode, and watched episode cards dim evenly. All packages are built by the public release workflow.

Fixed:

• Repeated background conversion. 0.5.4's check for changed 0.4 account data could give a different answer for the same data because it rebuilt a preferences archive before fingerprinting it. This triggered unnecessary conversion and account uploads, including during playback. The check now fingerprints the original legacy fields consistently and ignores native fields rewritten by routine sync. Unchanged routine syncs skip conversion after it succeeds. Genuine legacy changes still convert, and separately linked Stremio profile accounts retain their periodic 30-minute refresh. Removing this repeated work also reduces competition with opening your account.
• Hero trailers never started on Home and title pages on iPhone, iPad and Mac, or on title pages on Apple TV. The clip waited for a step that never ran. It runs now.
• Mac and iPad open a series on your episode. A long season opened on episode 1. The episode grid now scrolls to the episode in progress, or the next one after the episode you last played.
• Watched episode cards are dimmer and clean. The whole card darkens and loses its colour evenly, instead of fading into a smeared double image.

Changed:

• Less background polling, with live updates retained. A newer-change notification over the live sync connection still triggers a pull immediately. While that connection is responding, the fallback check runs every five minutes instead of every 3 seconds. If it disconnects or goes silent for 75 seconds, frequent fallback checks resume.
• A bigger Home billboard on Mac, running down to just above Customize.

Android:

Android checks for missed changes every five minutes while its live sync connection is up, instead of every 3 seconds.

VortX is Apple first. The Android APK is still an early technical preview rather than the finished app, so expect missing features and rough edges.

Please test:

• Use the app for a few minutes after the first launch, then watch something and check menu, tap and player responsiveness. With unchanged legacy data, the diagnostics log should no longer repeatedly show legacy_conversion run reason=changed. A first conversion, genuine legacy edits or a linked-account refresh can still produce a conversion entry.
• Close and reopen the app: the splash screen should be shorter than on 0.5.4.
• Leave Home open: the featured billboard should play its trailer muted.
• On Mac or iPad, open a series you are partway through: the episode list should open on your episode.
• Check that watched episodes look dimmed and clean.

Install:

Android phone, tablet and TV. VortX-0.5.5-full-mpv-universal.apk includes VortX Player. VortX-0.5.5-play-media3-universal.apk is the Media3 variant. Each APK contains both the phone and the Android TV interface. Choose the variant you already use so it installs over your current version. The Play bundle is also attached for its distribution workflow.

The Apple and Android packages were built by the release workflow from the v0.5.5-rc.1 tag, the same commit as v0.5.5. SHA256SUMS-ci.txt lists a SHA-256 checksum for each Apple package so you can confirm your download is intact; check the Android packages with SHA256SUMS-android.txt and SIGNING_PROVENANCE.txt.
