Подход повторяет то, что сделали авторы GTA V-портов (kevinerikjs/gta5-ios-port, c22dev/muguet) — берём у них проверенную сборочно-установочную обвязку.

Приложение показывает на экране:

• версию нативного ядра (компилируется C++20 под arm64);
• реальную силу балки, посчитанную на телефоне по модели RoR;
• лимит памяти, который iOS выдаёт приложению — от него зависят графика и пресеты.

Если эти числа видны на iPhone — конвейер работает, и дальше вопрос только в объёме порта.

versions.localizedDescription:
Unsigned, ad-hoc-signed RoR IPA for arm64 iPhone/iPad, built from 418211f8a.

Files (release-dependent):

• RoR-ios.ipa - the full game, ~112 MB. Ships its data in RoR.app/rorres/ (not resources/ - see below).
• RoR-ios-lite.ipa - the same app with the content-only archives dropped (meshes/textures/sounds/caelum/SkyX/ hydrax), ~40 MB. Every archive the startup path loads is kept, so it launches exactly like the full build - this is what makes it a usable launch diagnostic.
• RoR-ios-tiny.ipa - NOT the game. Shares Info.plist/signature/packaging with the game. Installs and launches (green screen).
• RoR-ios-bin.ipa - diagnostic (only on 'diag' tag). Real RoR binary, no data directory at all. The known-good baseline.
• RoR-ios-res0.ipa - diagnostic (only on 'diag' tag). bin plus a single file in resources/. The known-BAD reference.
• RoR-ios-res0r.ipa - diagnostic (only on 'diag' tag). bin plus the same single file, in rorres/ instead. What the fix does.

Why the directory is called rorres:

An .app whose bundle contains a top-level directory named resources (or Resources - the check is case-insensitive) is refused by the iOS installer with the generic "Unable to Install", while the very same directory under any other name (zzz/, Base.lproj/, rorres/) installs and runs. Measured on device: bin - no directory -> installs zzz/rotest.txt -> installs Base.lproj/rotest.txt -> installs resources/rotest.txt -> refused Resources/rotest.txt -> refused.

codesign is what flips. With a resources/ (or Resources/) directory present it switches its resource rules to the macOS "resource envelope" set - rules=^Resources/, plus a '^[^/]+$ -> nested' rule in rules2 - and iOS will not install a bundle sealed that way. With any other directory name it keeps the plain ^.* rules that iOS accepts. The ad-hoc signature was never the problem: an unsigned variant with resources/ is refused just the same.

If the game installs but crashes right after launching:

It now writes Documents/ror-trace.log - one line per startup phase, plus every OGRE log line and, if it dies, the reason (SIGSEGV, or the uncaught exception's message). That file is flushed line by line with write(2), so it is complete even when the process is killed mid-line. Open it on the phone: Files app -> On My iPhone -> Rigs of Rods -> ror-trace.log. The last lines are the interesting ones. The same folder holds RigsOfRods/logs/RoR.log, which OGRE writes - but that one is buffered and loses its tail on a crash, so prefer ror-trace.log.

Hand the file itself to ESIGN / Sideloadly / SideStore - it is served as a plain file, nothing to unpack. An .ipa is a zip whose root contains Payload/.

CHECK THE DOWNLOAD BEFORE INSTALLING.

A truncated download makes every installer fail, and the error looks like a build problem ("Truncated input file", "Unable to Install"). Compare the byte size of the file you downloaded with the list below; if it differs by even one byte, download the file again.

apps.name: Proton Stream
apps.subtitle: a client to stream videos (shows, movies) from proton drive
apps.localizedDescription:
proton-stream:

A Netflix-style cross-platform client for Proton Drive public links.

Paste a share URL and its password; get a browsable, streamable library. No Proton account, no server to host, no download step — episodes start playing in seconds and the seek bar works.

Built on proton-sdk-rs, a pure-Rust Proton Drive SDK.

Why it works:

A Proton Drive file's content blocks are each a self-contained PGP packet decrypted under one shared session key. There is no sequential streaming session to resume, so seeking costs exactly the blocks the seek lands on — a 2 GB episode is playable without downloading 2 GB of it.

Status:

An iOS 17+ client under ios/ is a SwiftUI port of the Android one over the same Rust engine, built as an unsigned .ipa for SideStore or AltStore; see.

apps.name: S5LBox
apps.subtitle: Classic iPhone OS
apps.localizedDescription:
S5LBox:

Classic iPhone OS. On your iPhone.

Slide to unlock. Open an old favorite. Make it yours again.

S5LBox brings the iPhone 3G and its original iPhone OS 3.1.3 to your iPhone. It's the real operating system, running inside an app—not a theme or a recreation. Your iPhone doesn't need to be jailbroken.

What you can do:

• Rediscover the classics. Explore the familiar Home screen, built-in apps, and compatible apps from the early days of iPhone.

• Bring your apps. Import .ipa files directly or put them in S5LBox's IPAs folder in Files. Choose what to install, one app at a time, without closing the running machine.

versions.localizedDescription:
Classic iPhone OS. On your iPhone.

The first public release of S5LBox: the iPhone 3G's iPhone OS 3.1.3 running inside an iOS app. This release is experimental; compatibility and performance are still being improved.

Firmware and first-run setup:

• Native first-run setup with progress, cancellation, errors and retry paths.

• Import an existing IPSW as an alternative. Selection is handled immediately, without reopening Settings or choosing the file a second time.
• Keep firmware details and manual overrides in Advanced settings. Skip setup once firmware is configured. No Apple firmware is bundled.

Machines, storage and controls:

• Create multiple independent machines, with long-press actions to rename, duplicate or delete them.
• Save and resume running sessions, or shut down for a fresh boot. Keep machine files accessible through the Files app.
• Use an 8 GiB virtual disk for new machines by default, with 2 and 4 GiB alternatives under Advanced. Sparse storage avoids allocating the full capacity immediately; guest data and saved sessions still use real storage.
• Modern emulator toolbar and a separate device-controls sheet for Home, sleep/wake, silent mode, volume, pause, restart and Save & close.
• Separate app settings from running-machine settings; keep the legacy interface available in Advanced.
• Pause in the background by default. Provide Force Power Off for guests that cannot complete an ordinary shutdown, including during boot.
• Use guest shutdown confirmation before restarting a running machine. Forced power-off remains an unclean stop and can lose unsaved work.

Guest apps and jailbreak:

• A Files-visible IPAs folder and in-app import, with individual app selection and real IPA icons, including supported legacy optimized PNG artwork.
• Install apps while the guest is running through virtual USB, pairing, AFC and the guest's installation_proxy service—not by editing its live disk.
• Installation progress, cancellation, guest verification errors and per-machine pairing identities.
• Guided guest jailbreak with Cydia, centered preparation progress and automatic entry into the machine afterward.
• First-boot setup performs a respring. The completion notice explains that Cydia may appear afterward and Packages may need a guest reboot.
• Packages helper setup is included with jailbreak by default, with an Advanced opt-out and a setup path for existing jailbroken machines.

Built-in Packages:

• Native package browsing, categories, search, sources, installed packages and available updates.

• Install, update and remove packages using the running guest's own dpkg and maintainer scripts. Unsupported dependency plans are refused rather than silently applied.
• Handle supported package finish requests for respring or reboot after changes, with progress and connection-recovery feedback.
• First-use helper setup and first-boot waiting are integrated into Packages; missing setup is not treated as a successful connection.

Emulation, networking and audio:

• ARMv6 guest execution with a no-JIT shipping path; no host jailbreak or JIT activation is required to run the emulator.
• Experimental MBX graphics enabled by default for new machines, with the existing software-rendering configuration retained for machines that use it.

• Experimental audio playback and microphone input, guest digital volume/mute, host audio-session handling and saved audio-device state.
• Microphone access enabled by default subject to iOS permission, with an Advanced opt-out. Declining permission does not block setup or boot.

Reliability fixes included in 1.0.0:

• Fix virtual USB reconnection after Save & close for both Packages and live IPA installation. Wake a sleeping guest for pending service work, and detect controller resets instead of mistaking cleared interrupts for a completed handshake.

• Improve jailbreak/helper first-boot recovery, stale filesystem metadata handling and protection of referenced disk blocks during supported stopped maintenance operations.

• Fix firmware picker/import state handling, setup progress presentation, retained setup state and the separation of everyday and Advanced controls.
• Include regression coverage for USB transport, installation, storage, firmware preparation, input, audio and package operations.

Compatibility and known limitations:

• Host requirement: an arm64 iOS device running iOS 13 or later. Physical-device validation has focused on iPhone 6s Plus with iOS 15.8.5; it does not establish identical behavior on every supported host version or device.

• Apps and tweaks must support this guest. Copy-protected IPAs cannot be installed; some otherwise compatible apps require AppSync inside the guest.
• Graphics, audio, input latency and performance remain experimental. Not all hardware, apps, tweaks, media formats or audio routes are supported, and original-device animation speed is not guaranteed.
• Packages is not a complete replacement for every Cydia/APT dependency plan. Unsupported plans may require Cydia. Guest scripts and initial jailbreak configuration can still take time; first boot may need a respring or reboot.
• Back up important machine data before experimenting. An interrupted installation can have an uncertain outcome; reconnecting does not undo it.

Installation:

Apple firmware, machine disks and test-device data are not part of the release assets.

ico-pc:

This is ICO (Sony Computer Entertainment, 2001) made to run as a normal program on a Windows or Linux PC, the Steam Deck, 64-bit ARM Linux handhelds, Android phones and tablets, iPhones and Apple-silicon Macs. It runs the game's own code, so it plays, sounds and feels like the PAL PlayStation 2 game. There are extras, such as a sharper picture, widescreen and smoother motion. The sharper picture, widescreen and the other picture extras stay off until you turn them on, and the frame rate is not held to the PS2's unless you choose Original. The mouse camera starts on.

versions.localizedDescription:
New:

• The log now says where the graphics time goes with Direct3D 12 too, as it already did with Vulkan: the lines written every 10 seconds show the time the graphics card spent and how much work it was given.
• The log now reports how the sound output is doing: how it was opened, and, every 10 seconds while the sound plays at the sound device's own pace (the usual way), whether it ever ran short. It also notes each time the game cuts a sound off at once and how loud that sound was. If you hear clicks or stutters, send the log with your report.

Fixed:

• The sound keeps playing through short loading pauses, and it no longer clicks when the picture falls behind. When the game stops for longer, the sound pauses with it instead of running ahead. This is for Windows, Linux, Android and Mac. A short click when you leave a room can still be the game stopping its own sounds, as it does on the PlayStation 2.
• On phones and other devices that cannot draw every picture in time at the chosen settings, the game keeps its normal speed by showing fewer pictures, instead of slowing down and catching up in jumps (at every frame rate except Original).
• On a Mac the game is now fast with anti-aliasing off. It used a slower way of mixing colours, which made the game only feel smooth with anti-aliasing on. The only cost is that a few blended colours can be one shade lighter than on the PlayStation 2.
• The glow, the depth of field and the screen softening are now drawn at the PlayStation 2's size at every resolution, as on the console; at 2x and above they look as coarse as they do there. The Glow size setting is gone.
• The 3D scenery is drawn by a new method that gives the same picture. If a graphics driver cannot handle it, the game notices at start and goes back to the old way by itself.

apps.localizedDescription:
JSRF Unleashed:

Jet Set Radio Future, running natively on Mac, Windows, Linux, Android, iPhone and iPad. Not an emulator — the game's own code, statically recompiled into C and built as a native application.

This project is about one game. It is not an Xbox emulator and it will not run other Xbox titles. Everything here — the graphics translation, the audio path, the file layout, the per-function fixes — is aimed at getting Jet Set Radio Future right. If you want to run Xbox games in general, you want xemu; if you want to port a different Xbox title, you want the toolkit this is built on.

versions.localizedDescription:
Jet Set Radio Future, natively on Mac, Windows, Linux, Android, iPhone and iPad. You need your own copy of the game (the USA release): these downloads are the engine only.

Android: on-screen controls and controllers on more phones:

Two players saw the intro play with no on-screen controls, and their Bluetooth controllers (an Xbox Series X controller, an 8BitDo Ultimate 2) did nothing. Many phones list one of their own parts as a gamepad: the device their fingerprint reader or side buttons send keys through declares gamepad buttons. The app counted it as a controller and hid the on-screen controls, and it was also opened first, as player 1's controller, so a real controller went in as player 2's, which the game does not read.

A device now counts as a controller only if it has a stick, or a d-pad that reports as one. On those phones the on-screen controls show, and a controller connected to them is player 1's. The log (Android/data/com.jumatt.jsrfunleashed/files/Logs/last-run.log) now says what the app made of each device Android calls a gamepad, and whether the on-screen controls are showing: if your phone still misbehaves, those [PAD] lines are what to send.

Tested in the Android emulator with a stand-in for such a phone part, there from the start, and a controller connected 20 seconds in that pressed Start and A. With 0.4.6 the on-screen controls were missing and the controller did nothing; with 0.4.7 the controls showed, went away when the controller connected, and the controller started the game.

The APK installs over the previous one. Only the Android download is new: the others are 0.4.6's, unchanged (0.4.6 fixed the black city in the Skyscraper District and Pharaoh Park on every platform).

apps.localizedDescription:
🎯 What is this?:

A port of the open-source IW4L engine to iOS. It does not contain the game: it reads the game files you already own on PC. Think of it as a new player for files you have.

📊 Where it stands:

• ✅ Runs natively on iPhone (Rust + Bevy + Metal).
• ✅ Reaches the main menu. Touch works as a click and a PS4 controller works.
• ✅ On an iPhone 17 Pro Max (6 GB granted to the app) full matches with bots run: watch the clip, by treuenten.

versions.localizedDescription:
IW4 Pocket 0.3.6:

Tested on one phone (iPhone 13 Pro Max, about 3 GB for the app): the lobby and in-match bot rows work and mp_rust loads, but a match still ends when iOS closes the app for memory after a few minutes. This release does not fix that. It adds bots you can add in the lobby and during a match, an option to leave out weapon camo skins, a shorter options menu, and new bot names.

Bots (issues #4 and #6).

• Lobby: a BOTS row in game setup, before the match (0 to 10).
• During a match: open the Options menu (Start) and tap Add 1 bot or Add 5 bots. Only the host adds bots; for everyone else the rows do nothing. If the rows do not show up, send iw4l-boot.log: it lists the menus it looked at.
• IW4L_BOTS=5 in iw4l-env.txt still sets how many bots a match starts with, and IW4L_CMDS=map mp_rust; bot add 5 works as before (only map, bot, and set/seta on match and bot rules). Neither has a row in the options menu.
• New bot names (2009-2010 style and a few memes), up to 15 characters.
• Credits: IW4L_BOTS by LemonMoo (Cade Palmer), the lobby bot row by AdrianTomasDiez. Both cherry-picked with their authorship, changed to share one value.

Options menu.

• IW4 Pocket options now has two pages: the first with the settings that matter most (profile, render scale, frame limit, texture size, lean shaders, weapon camo skins) and a second with the rest. "Free spare memory" is gone: in tests it gave back 0 MiB. Old IW4L_HEAP_RELIEF lines in iw4l-env.txt are ignored.
• Weapon camo skins (Auto keeps them, Skip leaves them out). The log has a camouflage: line saying what was kept or left out. Measured on the 13 Pro Max with the same map: Skip removed all 8360 + 8360 camo models, but memory after loading was the same (2511 MiB with Skip, 2512 MiB with the camos kept). So it is not a memory saver; it only leaves the camos out. Idea and first code by mk2rs2000.

SideStore source.

• Add https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MarkusSela/IW4-Pocket/main/source.json in SideStore (Sources, +). Test versions say TEST.

For phones with about 3 GB for the app: set Render scale to 0.67 or 0.5. That helps a little; the app can still be closed by iOS during a match.

Please send iw4l-boot.log (and iw4l-boot.crash.log if the app closes) and say how you installed the app.

AI Agent · Boundaries · CLI ·.

Community ·.

It used to take six or seven services, six or seven configs, and a lot of effort to keep them all agreeing about the same library. Now it's just MovieClaw:

All-in-one has its trade-offs, and they're laid out honestly in Boundaries.

Native apps, with playback that rivals Infuse:

iPhone and iPad 0.9.0: A real iPad app:

MovieClaw now runs as a proper iPad app instead of an enlarged iPhone app, with a sidebar, larger title pages and free rotation. On iPhone, the Me tab is reorganized, and the AI chat lets you pick a model, search the web and keep you company while it works.

Your library, laid out for the bigger screen:

On iPad the app used to run in iPhone compatibility mode: a narrow window with phone-sized posters. Now it fills the screen and works in any orientation, Split View and Stage Manager. Update and open it on your iPad.

• A sidebar lists Home, Favorites, Subscriptions, Discover, Activity and Me, plus every library and your home collections. Each keeps its own place as you switch.
• Title pages use the Mac layout: a full-width backdrop with the title, details and actions at the bottom left and the cast at the bottom right.
• Posters have one width across home rows and walls, and sheets open as centered panels.
• The player follows how you hold the iPad. There is no rotate button, and Back always leaves the player.
• To switch accounts on iPad, use the people button (切换账号) at the top right of Me.
• In Split View or a narrow window, pages fall back to the iPhone layout.

Pick a model before you ask:

Starting a chat from the Me tab used whatever model you last picked on the new-conversation page, with no way to change it there. Now administrators can tap the small input box on Me to expand it: a model button below it lets you choose the model and its Thinking strength (思维链强度) for the new conversation, and your choice is remembered. If the server has a ChatGPT plan connected, its models are listed too.

• Administrators can connect web search from Me → Server → Server settings → AI Settings → Web search (网页搜索): choose Tavily, Exa or Brave Search, paste the key and tap the ✓ button (验证并保存).

• Touch buttons rescaled to 32x32, which mangled every glyph. They sit at their native 22x22 now and scale by whole multiples of it.
• The inventory and pause touch buttons rendering as blank plates.
• The touch layout, rebuilt to match Bedrock's: utility strip centred at the top, jump, sneak and interact down the right edge, sneak in the middle of the D-pad.
• The Linux memory readout assuming a 4 KiB page size.

Opentify:

A self-hosted personal music server with its own apps (web, iOS, Android, Windows). It plays your own music library, organises it with metadata from MusicBrainz and Deezer, and gives you a Spotify-like experience on your own hardware.

Osobní hudební server pro vlastní hardware. Rozhraní appky je česky.

Status: a personal hobby project, not released for use by others yet (see License). The app's interface is in Czech, there is no support, and things change without notice.
